statement_summary: Program meets FAR 52.204-21 for FCI systems and SP 800-171 Rev. 2 for CUI systems
Security program lead and CMMC Affirming Official designated in writing
Annual enterprise risk assessment using SP 800-30
Risk acceptance authority by level; no risk accepted that makes a federal representation inaccurate
Quarterly reporting to the audit committee
Annual policy and standard review
Written, risk-rated, time-limited exceptions; none against SP 800-171 or FAR requirements
Bank and EFT changes verified by call-back, second approver, and log; no override; first-payment hold
Owners told that remittance changes are never made by email alone
Vendor security review and terms before holding sensitive data; FedRAMP Moderate or equivalent for CUI cloud
Tier 1 vendors reassessed annually
Flowdown of FAR, DFARS 252.204-7012, and CMMC requirements; SPRS verification before award; no CUI before the steps
No covered Section 889 equipment provided, installed, rented, or used; manufacturer confirmed in writing
Federal representations only with evidence binder, independent reperformance, and counsel review
Annual independent assessment and SP 800-171A self-assessment
Security records kept 6 years; certified payroll records 3 years after the work
AI tools approved before use; no CUI; no AI changes to payment data
Sanctions in proportion to intent and harm
Unique accounts; no shared accounts
Role-based least privilege; SaaS company-administrator rights limited to IT
Separation of duties for payments and SAM EFT data
MFA everywhere; phishing-resistant MFA for CPE, administrators, executives, and payment roles; verified help desk resets
Same-day disable at termination; transfer removal; same-day CPE removal off FC-4
External users removed at closeout; A&E guests expire after 30 days
Quarterly access reviews; monthly CPE review; quarterly payment role review
Separate admin accounts with FIDO2; privileged access broker; break-glass tested quarterly
14-character passwords; default passwords changed before use
Managed devices only; CUI only from enclave laptops or virtual desktop clients; tablets enrolled
Remote access with MFA through managed points; no internet-facing router administration
Physical access: badges, trailer locks, CUI room, escorts, logs, key inventory
Vendor and MBSS remote access through the company gateway with named, recorded sessions
Incident response plan with BEC and CUI runbooks integrated with crisis management and legal
Immediate reporting by workforce, within 1 hour
Every incident logged and tracked
Bank recall and IC3 complaint the same day for payment diversion
Possible CUI incidents reviewed for compromise at once; discovery time recorded
DoD report within 72 hours; two medium assurance certificates; malware to DC3
Log export at incident start; images preserved 90 days; DoD access honored
Section 889 reports within 1 business day and 10 business days
Subcontractor incident numbers collected and assessed
Breach determinations for personal information and client systems; notices on time
Insurer notified through the carrier hotline before vendors are engaged
Annual exercise per runbook, including a DIBNet drill; annual role training
Lessons learned within 30 days
Six classification levels including CUI
CUI accepted only into the CPE; CUI found elsewhere treated as a possible incident
CUI flow limited to the distribution list; download and clipboard blocked; CUI RFIs in the CPE
Approved external systems list by data level; personal accounts prohibited
FIPS-validated cryptography for CUI; encryption for Restricted and FCI
Printed CUI: approved printers, numbered sets, CUI room, sealed transport, certified shredding
Marking check on every A&E CUI package
Sanitization with certificates before disposal or reuse
Encrypted, separated, immutable backups; quarterly restore tests
No CUI in any AI tool; other data only in approved AI tools
Client facility security details in the credential vault; deleted after handover
Retention schedule
Business use; limited personal use
Signed acknowledgment at hire and annually; CUI acknowledgment for CPE users
Awareness, payment-fraud, CUI role-based, and insider threat training; quarterly phishing exercises
Never act on a bank change received by email, text, or phone
CUI stays in the enclave; report CUI found elsewhere
No forwarding to personal accounts; no company data on personal devices
Lock screens, trailers, and the CUI room
No unapproved software, extensions, or USB storage
Report phishing, MFA prompts, and lost devices immediately
Approved AI tools only; never CUI
No posting of facility interiors, trailers, client security systems, or drawings
Approved commissioning laptops and gateway only in client buildings
